explain.say: Can you imagine a whole continent changing its flags in about 20 years? Between 1804 and 1824, most of Latin America broke free from Spain, Portugal and France. This timeline shows how. Let's travel along it.

explain.say: Look at 1810. In the Mexican town of Dolores, a priest named Miguel Hidalgo rang the church bell and called people to rise against Spanish rule. That call is called the Grito, the cry. Mexicans repeat it every year on the night of 15 September. Have you heard it?

faq.q: Why did Latin American colonies want independence?
faq.a: Many people born in the Americas, called criollos, resented rule from Spain and Portugal, taxes and trade limits. Ideas from the American and French revolutions spread, and Napoleon's invasion of Spain in 1808 weakened Spanish rule. Often power stayed with criollo elites, and Indigenous and enslaved people gained less.
A Venezuelan general and leader, called El Libertador, the Liberator. He led armies that freed much of northern South America from Spain, and Bolivia is named after him.
asks: Why is Bolivar called the Liberator?

faq.q: Who was Jose de San Martin?
faq.a: An Argentine general who led the Army of the Andes across the mountains in 1817 to free Chile, then helped free Peru, declaring its independence in 1821.
Unlike most of Latin America, Brazil's independence was led by a royal. On 7 September 1822, Prince Pedro, son of the Portuguese king, declared independence and became Emperor Pedro I.

faq.q: What is the Grito de Dolores?
faq.a: The cry of Dolores: Miguel Hidalgo's call to revolt in the town of Dolores in the early hours of 16 September 1810. Mexico celebrates its Independence Day on 16 September.

facts: The Battle of Ayacucho in 1824 ended major Spanish rule in South America.
Bolivia is named after Simon Bolivar.
